bibl.title: Attention gated networks: Learning to leverage salient regions in medical images

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether a network can be made to find the organ it is supposed to measure, instead of being handed a cropped region by a second network trained to find it
span.quote: We propose a novel attention gate (AG) model for medical image analysis that automatically learns to focus on target structures of varying shapes and sizes. Models trained with AGs implicitly learn to suppress irrelevant regions in an input image while highlighting salient features useful for a specific task. This enables us to eliminate the necessity of using explicit external tissue/organ localisation modules when using convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

span.label: whether a soft attention gate inside a single CNN can replace the cascade - a localisation model followed by a segmentation model - without losing accuracy or adding many parameters
span.quote: Methods for existing applications rely heavily on multi-stage, cascaded CNNs when the target organs show large inter-patient variation in terms of shape and size. Cascaded frameworks extract a region of interest (ROI) and make dense predictions on that particular ROI. The application areas include cardiac MRI, cardiac CT, abdominal CT segmentation, and lung CT nodule detection. However, this approach leads to excessive and redundant use of computational resources and model parameters; for instance, similar low-level features are repeatedly extracted by all models within the cascade.

span.label: a grid-based additive attention gate that drops into VGG or U-Net, learns where to look with no bounding boxes and no extra supervision, improves recall and precision on CT pancreas segmentation and fetal ultrasound plane detection, and is shown to beat simply making the baseline bigger
span.quote: We take the attention approach proposed by a step further by proposing grid-based gating that allows attention gates to be more specific to local regions. This improves performance compared to gating based on a global feature vector.

span.label: method
span.quote: To address this general problem, we propose a simple and yet effective solution, named attention gates (AGs). By incorporating AGs into standard CNN models, model parameters and intermediate feature maps are expected to be utilised more efficiently while minimising the necessity of cascaded models to solve localisation and classification tasks separately. In more detail, AGs automatically learn to focus on target structures without additional supervision. At test time, these gates generate soft region proposals implicitly on-the-fly and highlight salient features useful for a specific task. In return, the proposed AGs improve model sensitivity and accuracy for global and dense label predictions by suppressing feature activations in irrelevant regions. In this way, the necessity of using an external organ localisation module can be eliminated while maintaining the high prediction accuracy.

span.label: small, variable-shaped structures that a single-stage network misses, and the cascades built to hand it a cropped view of them - which repeat the same low-level features in every model of the chain
span.quote: Methods for existing applications rely heavily on multi-stage, cascaded CNNs when the target organs show large inter-patient variation in terms of shape and size. Cascaded frameworks extract a region of interest (ROI) and make dense predictions on that particular ROI. The application areas include cardiac MRI, cardiac CT, abdominal CT segmentation, and lung CT nodule detection. However, this approach leads to excessive and redundant use of computational resources and model parameters; for instance, similar low-level features are repeatedly extracted by all models within the cascade.

span.label: attention coefficients computed from a coarse gating signal and a finer feature map, applied multiplicatively, trained end-to-end with deep supervision at each scale; evaluated on two CT abdominal datasets and a 190k-frame ultrasound set
span.term: attention coefficients computed from a coarse gating signal and a finer feature map, applied multiplicatively, trained end-to-end with deep supervision at each scale; evaluated on two CT abdominal datasets and a 190k-frame ultrasound set
span.quote: Gating parameters are initialised so that attention gates pass through feature vectors at all spatial locations. Moreover, we do not require multiple training stages as in hard-attention based approaches therefore simplifying the training procedure.

span.label: a cascade spends a whole network learning where the organ is and then throws that network's features away; a gate computes the same decision from features the predictor already has, so the localisation costs 8% more parameters instead of a second model, and the low-level features are extracted once
span.quote: Methods for existing applications rely heavily on multi-stage, cascaded CNNs when the target organs show large inter-patient variation in terms of shape and size. Cascaded frameworks extract a region of interest (ROI) and make dense predictions on that particular ROI. The application areas include cardiac MRI, cardiac CT, abdominal CT segmentation, and lung CT nodule detection. However, this approach leads to excessive and redundant use of computational resources and model parameters; for instance, similar low-level features are repeatedly extracted by all models within the cascade.

span.label: the gating parameters start so that every feature vector passes at every location - the network begins as its own baseline and has to learn to suppress, which is why no multi-stage training schedule is needed and why any difference is attributable to what the gate learned rather than to where it started
span.term: a gate initialised to do nothing
span.quote: Gating parameters are initialised so that attention gates pass through feature vectors at all spatial locations. Moreover, we do not require multiple training stages as in hard-attention based approaches therefore simplifying the training procedure.

span.label: the gating signal is taken from a coarser grid, where the receptive field is large enough to know where the organ is, and applied to a finer map, where the resolution is enough to draw its boundary - which is the same division of labour a cascade makes between its two networks, done inside one
span.quote: We commonly observe that AGs initially have a uniform distribution and pass features at all spatial locations. This is gradually updated and localised towards the targeted organ boundaries. Additionally, at coarser scales AGs provide a rough outline of organs which are gradually refined at finer resolutions. Moreover, by training multiple AGs at each image scale, we observe that each AG learns to focus on a particular subset of organs.

span.label: softmax over the attention map produces sparse, intensity-sensitive attention, which is bad in ultrasound; sigmoid only rescales and lets more information through, and pays for it with gradient saturation. Neither is free and the paper reports both costs
span.term: a normalisation choice that trades sparsity against gradients
span.quote: We empirically observed and reported that using soft-max as the activation function tends to generate a map that is sparsely activated and is overly sensitive to local intensity changes. The latter is problematic as in ultrasound imaging, image quality is often low. In the classification setting, We found that dividing the activations by the sum of the activations helped generate attention map with larger contextual support. As demonstrated in the segmentation framework, Sigmoid function is a good alternative as it only normalises the range and allows more information to flow. However, we found that training is non-trivial due to the gradient saturation problem.

span.label: the attention map outlines the discriminant region and does not necessarily coincide with the entire object, so it localises without delineating
span.quote: We see that the network consistently focuses on the object of interest, consistent with the blue ground truth annotation. We note, however, attention map outlines the discriminant region; in particular, it does not necessarily coincide with the entire object. Nevertheless, as it does not guided backpropagation for localisation (a strategy in), attention models are advantageous for the real-time applications.

span.label: the comparison against 2D cascaded state-of-the-art models is called insufficient to draw a final conclusion, because the 3D model has context and the 2D models have resolution
span.quote: Lastly, we note that the presented quantitative comparisons between the Attention 3D-Unet and state-of-the-art 2D cascaded models might not be sufficient enough to draw a final conclusion, as the proposed approach takes advantage of rich contextual information in all spatial dimensions. On the other hand, the 2D models utilise the high resolution information present in axial CT planes without any downsampling.

span.label: softmax normalisation gives sparse, intensity-sensitive maps and sigmoid gives gradient saturation - the normalisation choice has no free option
span.quote: We empirically observed and reported that using soft-max as the activation function tends to generate a map that is sparsely activated and is overly sensitive to local intensity changes. The latter is problematic as in ultrasound imaging, image quality is often low. In the classification setting, We found that dividing the activations by the sum of the activations helped generate attention map with larger contextual support. As demonstrated in the segmentation framework, Sigmoid function is a good alternative as it only normalises the range and allows more information to flow. However, we found that training is non-trivial due to the gradient saturation problem.

span.label: training the attention mechanism is more complex than the baseline, and the most stable route was per-scale training followed by fine-tuning
span.quote: We noted that training the attention-mechanism was slightly more complex than the standard network architecture. In particular, we observed that the strategy employed to aggregate the attention maps at different scales affects both the learning of the attention mechanism itself and hence the performance. Having a loss term defined at each scale ensures that the network learns to attend at each scale. We observed that first training the network at each scale separately, followed by fine-tuning was the most stable approach to get the optimal performance.

span.label: residual connections around the gate gave no significant improvement in the segmentation experiments
span.quote: There is a vast body of literature in machine learning exploring different gating architectures. For example, highway networks make use of residual connections around the gate block to allow better gradient backpropagation and slightly softer attention mechanisms. Although our segmentation experiments with residual connections have not provided any significant performance improvement, future work will focus on this aspect to obtain a better training behaviour.

span.label: additive soft attention, carried from sentence-to-sentence machine translation into a convolutional network over medical images, and re-based on an image grid so the coefficients can be local
span.quote: We take the attention approach proposed by a step further by proposing grid-based gating that allows attention gates to be more specific to local regions. This improves performance compared to gating based on a global feature vector.

span.label: higher-capacity U-Net models trained and compared against the smaller gated model, rather than only against the same-size baseline
span.note: eliminates: the extra parameters as the explanation of the gain - a module that adds 8% capacity and improves DSC by 2-3% has to be shown to beat 8% more capacity spread uniformly, and it does at p = .007 · outcome: held
span.quote: In Table 1, we also report the number of trainable parameters for both models. We observe that by adding 8% extra capacity to the standard U-Net, the performance can be improved by 2-3% in terms of DSC. For a fair comparison, we also train higher capacity U-Net models and compare against the proposed model with smaller network size. The results shown in Table 2 demonstrate that the addition of AGs contributes more than simply increasing model capacity (uniformly) across all layers of the network (p = .007). Therefore, additional capacity should be used for AGs to localise tissues, in cases when AGs are used to reduce the redundancy of training multiple, individual models.

span.label: the same two models retrained at a smaller training size (30 images instead of 120)
span.note: eliminates: the improvement being an artefact of one data budget - if attention only helps when data is plentiful it is not solving the localisation problem it claims to · outcome: held
span.quote: In the second experiment, the same models are trained with fewer training images (30) to show that the performance improvement is consistent and significant for different sizes of training data (p = .01). For both approaches, we observe a performance drop on spleen DSC as the training size is reduced. The drop is less significant with the proposed framework. For kidney segmentation, the models achieve similar accuracy since the tissue contrast is higher.

span.label: models trained on CT-150 applied directly to the public CT-82 benchmark with no fine-tuning, before any adaptation is done
span.note: eliminates: the result being tied to one institution's data - the transfer is measured before the models are allowed to see the new distribution · outcome: held
span.quote: Initially, the models trained on CT-150 dataset are directly applied to CT-82 dataset to observe the applicability of the two models on different datasets. The corresponding results (BFT) are given in Table 3. U-Net model outperforms traditional atlas techniques although it was trained on a disjoint dataset. Moreover, the attention model performs consistently better in pancreas segmentation across different datasets.

span.label: both models also trained from scratch on 61 CT-82 images, in addition to the fine-tuned and directly-applied conditions
span.note: eliminates: pre-training on the private dataset as a hidden advantage in the public benchmark comparison · outcome: held
span.quote: Additionally, we trained the two models from scratch (SCR) with 61 training images randomly selected from the CT-82 dataset. Similar to the results on CT-150 dataset, AGs improve the segmentation accuracy and lower the surface distances (p = .03) due to increased recall rate of pancreas pixels (p = .09).

span.label: 5-fold cross-validation on CT-82 with the Attention U-Net, reported with its standard deviation
span.note: eliminates: a single favourable train/test split - the spread of 6.23 DSC is the size of the effect being claimed, and reporting it makes that visible · outcome: held
span.quote: Lastly, we performed 5-fold cross-validation on the CT-82 dataset using the Attention U-Net for a better comparison, which achieved 81.48 ± 6.23 DSC for pancreas labels.

span.label: conditional random field post-processing deliberately NOT applied, and said so, although the comparison methods use it
span.note: eliminates: post-processing absorbing or masking the gate's contribution - the measured difference is the module's in an isolated setting, at the cost of a lower absolute number · outcome: held
span.quote: It is important to note that, postprocessing (e.g. using conditional random field) is not utilised in our framework as the experiments mainly focus on quantification of performance improvement brought by AGs in an isolated setting. Similarly, residual and dense connections can be used as in in conjunction with AGs to improve the segmentation results.

span.label: ultrasound frames cropped to the central 208 x 272 so the network cannot read the annotations the scanner prints around the image

span.quote: data was cropped to central 208 × 272 to prevent the network from learning the surrounding annotations shown in the ultrasound scan screen.

span.label: gating parameters initialised so that the gates pass every feature vector at every location, making the network start as its own baseline
span.note: eliminates: that the attention gates help only because they change the initialisation - starting open makes the network its own baseline at step zero · outcome: held
span.quote: Gating parameters are initialised so that attention gates pass through feature vectors at all spatial locations. Moreover, we do not require multiple training stages as in hard-attention based approaches therefore simplifying the training procedure.

span.label: class imbalance handled by weighted sampling for classification and a Dice loss for segmentation, in both the attention and the baseline networks
span.note: eliminates: the dominant background class carrying the score, and any difference between the two networks being a difference in how each one met the imbalance · outcome: held
span.quote: The datasets used in this manuscript contain large class imbalance issue that needs to be addressed. For ultrasound dataset, due to the nature of screening process, the background label dominates the dataset. To address this, we used a weighted sampling strategy, where we matched the probability of sampling one of the foreground labels to the probability of sampling a background label. For the segmentation models, the class imbalance problem is tackled using the Sorensen-Dice loss defined over all semantic classes. Dice loss is experimentally shown to be less sensitive to class imbalance in segmentation tasks.

AG-Sononet reduces false positive examples because the gating mechanism suppresses background noise and forces the network to make the prediction based on class-specific features. As the capacity of Sononet is increased, the gap between the methods are tightened, but we note that the performance of AG-Sononet is also close to the one of Sononet with double the capacity.

span.label: each attention gate learns to focus on a particular subset of organs, starting from a uniform distribution and localising over training
span.term: each attention gate learns to focus on a particular subset of organs, starting from a uniform distribution and localising over training
span.quote: We commonly observe that AGs initially have a uniform distribution and pass features at all spatial locations. This is gradually updated and localised towards the targeted organ boundaries. Additionally, at coarser scales AGs provide a rough outline of organs which are gradually refined at finer resolutions. Moreover, by training multiple AGs at each image scale, we observe that each AG learns to focus on a particular subset of organs.

span.label: probabilistic, end-to-end differentiable attention using standard backpropagation without posterior sampling - as against hard attention, which crops and needs reinforcement learning
span.quote: Trainable attention, on the other hand, is enforced by design and categorised as hard- and soft-attention. Hard attention, e.g. iterative region proposal and cropping, is often non-differentiable and relies on reinforcement learning for parameter updates, which makes model training more difficult. used recursive hard-attention to detect anomalies in chest X-ray scans. Contrarily, soft attention is probabilistic, end-to-end differentiable, and utilises standard back-propagation without need for posterior sampling.

span.label: what an attention map outlines - the part of the object the classifier uses, which the authors state does not necessarily coincide with the entire object
span.quote: We see that the network consistently focuses on the object of interest, consistent with the blue ground truth annotation. We note, however, attention map outlines the discriminant region; in particular, it does not necessarily coincide with the entire object. Nevertheless, as it does not guided backpropagation for localisation (a strategy in), attention models are advantageous for the real-time applications.

span.label: extra capacity added to the standard U-Net by the attention gates, for a 2-3% DSC improvement
span.quote: In Table 1, we also report the number of trainable parameters for both models. We observe that by adding 8% extra capacity to the standard U-Net, the performance can be improved by 2-3% in terms of DSC. For a fair comparison, we also train higher capacity U-Net models and compare against the proposed model with smaller network size. The results shown in Table 2 demonstrate that the addition of AGs contributes more than simply increasing model capacity (uniformly) across all layers of the network (p = .007). Therefore, additional capacity should be used for AGs to localise tissues, in cases when AGs are used to reduce the redundancy of training multiple, individual models.

span.label: mean pancreas DSC over 5-fold cross-validation on CT-82, with a standard deviation of 6.23
span.quote: Lastly, we performed 5-fold cross-validation on the CT-82 dataset using the Attention U-Net for a better comparison, which achieved 81.48 ± 6.23 DSC for pancreas labels.
